newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan MOF will act properly to avoid instability.
newsitem.headline: Japan MOF will act properly to avoid instability.

text.p: Japan's Finance Ministry will act appropriately to avoid instability in the financial system both at home and aboard, Vice Finance Minister Tadashi Ogawa told a news conference on Thursday.
"We must act properly and watch carefully so that abroad," he said.
He added that efforts by individual Japanese financial institutions to stabilise their businesses would form a pillar in maintaining financial-system stability.
Ogawa also said that efforts by individual banks to strengthen their businesses would lead to protection of depositors.
He said Japanese banks were dealing with their bad-loan problems and also face financial deregulation steps in coming years.
"Market participants and investors are watching to see how each financial institution will deal with these issues. We will keep a close watch on the situation."

Asked about a comment on Wednesday by a senior official of the ruling Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) that investors in bank debentures may be protected using public funds, Ogawa said that long-term credit banks should first work to secure the credibility and reliability of the instruments.
He said the government would support these efforts.
Ogawa said that in theory the Deposit Insurance Corp of Japan did not include protection for investors in bank debentures.
Asked about any plans to privatise the state-owned Japan to privatise (the bank)."

He said government lending agencies tended to supplement private financial institutions in that they were willing to lend to projects that were in the national interest but not necessarily highly profitable.

As well as speaking of the possibility of public funds being used to protect investors, the LDP official, Taku Yamasaki, was quoted by Jiji news agency as saying that there was talk that one of the long-term credit banks, Nippon Credit Bank Ltd, should be merged with the government-run Japan Development Bank after privatisation of the latter.
Yamasaki is the LDP"s policy chief.
Last week, a senior NCB official denied market rumours that the bank may be near collapse and said there was no reason to worry about the bank"s liquidity.
